slot: Your question, plus the daily report
summary: The S&P 500 ended September down 0.25% at 7,651.54, capping what Bloomberg called the worst month since June. The market opened higher on softer inflation news, then sold off hard in the final hour as the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.29%, spooking investors who worry that high borrowing costs will squeeze corporate profits. Gold held near its highs and bitcoin was essentially flat at 83,709. Friday brings the big one: the monthly jobs report, which will tell the Fed whether the economy is still too hot to cut rates.
